title: A Shark Under Two Feet Long Took Bites Out of Nuclear Submarines
subject: cookiecutter shark

scenes.text: A shark under two feet long blinded American nuclear submarines.
The cookiecutter shark. In the 1970s, it kept chewing the rubber-covered sonar domes of US subs.
Oil leaked out and the subs lost their sonar. The Navy had to cover the domes with fiberglass.
It isn't hunting subs. It clamps on, spins its body, and cuts a round plug of flesh out of whales, dolphins and tuna.
The wounds are about two inches across and two and a half inches deep.
And the glow under its throat looks like a small fish. Big predators swim up for a snack. They're the meal.

description:
A cookiecutter shark, under two feet long, chewed the sonar domes of American nuclear submarines in the 1970s.
It clamps onto whales, dolphins and tuna, spins, and cuts out a round plug of flesh about two inches across. A dark collar on its throat looks like a small fish and lures big predators in.
Which deep-sea animal would you least want to meet? Comment below.
first_comment: Cookiecutters rise from below about 3,000 feet to feed at night. Would you swim in the open ocean after this?
